abstract: Fear memories formed in early life are forgotten rapidly, but the circuits that delay stable memory expression are not well defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) projects to the basolateral amygdala (BLA), and both regions mature late, yet the behavior, anatomy and physiology of this pathway have rarely been examined together across development. We trained mice in cued auditory fear conditioning at postnatal day (P) 14-15, P20-21 or P59-70 and tested tone-evoked freezing 1, 7 and 14 days later. Early juvenile mice showed no cue-specific freezing at any memory retrieval time points, late juvenile mice showed it at 7 and 14 days but not at 1 day, and adults showed it at all retrieval time points. In separate mice, mPFC axons were low in the BLA at P11 and more abundant at P38 and P90, and light-evoked prelimbic synaptic responses in BLA principal neurons were not detectable at P11 but were robust at P35 and P70. Spontaneous synaptic currents and intrinsic excitability of BLA principal neurons, and excitability of prelimbic principal neurons and interneurons, also changed between P11 and adulthood. These data identify a protracted period of mPFC-BLA circuit maturation that overlaps the emergence of cue-specific fear and define the ages at which candidate mechanisms can be tested.
